I don't know if you've seen this already perhaps, but for what it's worth, this is (unofficially) semi-supported already, as I use `JPH::FixedConstraint` when you use a `HingeJoint3D` or `SliderJoint3D` but leave its upper/lower limits the same (e.g. both at zero).

With that said, that might perhaps have been a questionable thing to do on my part, and something I've been wanting to see replaced with a dedicated joint like this eventually. I think it makes sense to add this type of joint to the shared interface, since it seems fairly prevalent (if not ubiquitous) among the physics engines out there.

However, given the current experimental status of the Jolt module, and the theoretical possibility of Godot Physics remaining the default 3D physics engine for a good while longer, I do think the no-op implementation for it here is a bit problematic. I can't say I would know how to implement it for Godot Physics myself though, unfortunately.

There's also the question of whether this should then be added to the 2D physics interface as well (ideally also with an accompanying implementation for Godot Physics I guess).

@mihe indeed, I mostly put this here so its not lost, I did the work but as I said, it didn't resolve my issue. 

Long term I don't think we can avoid Jolt and Godot physics to diverge, so at some point we'll need to discuss how we're going to deal with those sort of issues. Else we'll always have a weakest link situation. Just glancing through what Jolt supports that Godot currently doesn't, there are some gems there we really don't want to leave by the wayside.

So far I'm enjoying using Jolt but there are some weird things that aren't working properly for me, or at least not as I expect them to work. I'm not sure where to go with questions about those issues.
Though XR has it's unique requirements that so far I've found few physics engines really catering for.

> Long term I don't think we can avoid Jolt and Godot physics to diverge, so at some point we'll need to discuss how we're going to deal with those sort of issues. Else we'll always have a weakest link situation. Just glancing through what Jolt supports that Godot currently doesn't, there are some gems there we really don't want to leave by the wayside.

It's not just about Godot Physics though, since anything added to the shared interface affects any physics engine extensions (current or future) out there as well. I'm certainly not advocating for Jolt-specific features to never be added to Godot, but it should ideally be done in a way where it doesn't impact the shared interface too much. The relatively simplistic implementation of Godot Physics, and I guess also having shared the interface with Bullet in 3.x, has arguably helped shape an interface that's already widely applicable to a lot of physics engines out there (with the joints being a notable exception I guess) and it would seem unfortunate to worsen that situation now.

There have been discussions about allowing physics servers to act on behalf of things like `Object._validate_property` for the default physics nodes, to allow them to modify the default physics nodes to their liking, which (as I understand) already has some precedence in Godot with things like `OpenXRCompositionLayer`.

More Jolt-specific nodes (e.g. `JPH::PathConstraint`) is still somewhat of an unsolved problem though. I'm not sure what the best approach might be there, short of registering/implementing it from the Jolt module and prefixing it with `Jolt...`, like I did with the extension, and only add its implementation details on a `JoltPhysicsServer3D` instead.

> So far I'm enjoying using Jolt but there are some weird things that aren't working properly for me, or at least not as I expect them to work. I'm not sure where to go with questions about those issues.

If you find them to be deal-breaking (or just annoying) discrepancies when compared to Godot Physics (or just in general even) I would suggest you just report an issue for them here. Part of the reason for making the Jolt module experimental is exactly to find these points of friction and either smooth them out somehow or at least clearly document them.

> So far I'm enjoying using Jolt but there are some weird things that aren't working properly for me, or at least not as I expect them to work. I'm not sure where to go with questions about those issues.

If you have specific Jolt questions you can always post them at https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics/discussions

@mihe @jrouwe sorry for the late reply, the problem for me at the moment is simply not knowing what the constraining factor is.

I had pretty much given up on Godot physics to try and replicate the more advanced physics features found in many XR games because it just didn't cut it. I'm getting much closer with Jolt than I've had in the past.

But its hard to say whether the issues I'm running into are due to the approach taken, shortcomings in Godots integration of Jolt, Jolt itself, or simply my expectations.

When I have some free time I'm planning on making a few test projects that showcase some of the issues I'm running into as discussion points to see if I can come to the bottom of what exactly is missing/incorrect.
